sportspicker_core/awards.py: A contest contributes exactly its budget. For any round, the points awarded across the field sum to that round's pot exactly, to the ten-thousandth of a point — whatever normalization strategy is chosen, however many members played, and however they scored, including a round nobody scored in, where the pot is split evenly rather than forfeited. Amounts are Decimals in ten-thousandths; where a division does not come out even, the leftover units go one at a time to the largest remainders, ties to the lowest membership id, so the same inputs always give the same split whatever order they arrive in. A weight for a member outside the field, a negative or non-finite weight, and a float amount are refused, never reinterpreted. A contest's budget is divided across every round it contains, played or not, so a round's value is knowable in advance and never repriced mid-season, and the round pots sum to the budget exactly: leftover ten-thousandths go to the earliest rounds. A single-round contest pays its whole budget in that round; a contest with no rounds pays nothing rather than dividing by zero. Ranking is competition-style: tied members share a rank and the following place is skipped. The raw baseline strategy deliberately bypasses budgets and must keep doing so. min_participants gates on members who SCORED, not members who merely submitted picks, and a field landing exactly on the minimum has met it. A minimum must say whether a short field scales or voids the pot; neither is assumed.
sportspicker_core/budgets.py: Every contest carries its own budget, an amount rather than a share of a fixed total, so adding a contest never devalues the ones already in the group. A contest without a budget is refused, naming the contest; there is no amount to fall back to. An explicit budget, including zero, is used as given, and a repeated contest takes its last budget rather than a sum. Budgets are exact amounts in ten-thousandths; a float budget is refused rather than converted, and a negative one is refused.
sportspicker_core/registry.py: Every registered sport resolves to the scoring engine its module names; a module must name one, a winner-pick sport included. An unregistered sport is refused with UnknownSportError rather than scored by a fallback, because binary scoring for a sport that scores differently produces a plausible but wrong table. Registering a slug that is already registered is refused unless replacement is asked for explicitly. A sport's result detail is declared as a pair — where the caller finds it and the dataclass the engine receives — and half a declaration is refused at registration.
sportspicker_core/modules.py: The built-in sport modules are registered by importing the package, not by each entry point remembering to do it — the application, the command line and the tests are separate doors, and forgetting one would leave a sport unregistered and every attempt to score it refused.
sportspicker_core/engines/base.py: A scoring engine turns one member's PickInput and the match's MatchOutcome into points, and every engine honors that contract identically so a new sport can be added without touching the award arithmetic. Engines accept only those plain dataclasses, never an object merely shaped like them, and a malformed input — the wrong type, or a pick naming a team that was not in the match — raises rather than scoring a quiet zero.
sportspicker_core/engines/inputs.py: The scoring inputs are plain frozen dataclasses with no defaults: absence is stated with None, never assumed. A match outcome has exactly two distinct sides, and its winner is the higher-scoring side, or nobody for a draw or a match without both scores.
sportspicker_core/engines/binary.py: A correct outcome pick scores; an incorrect one does not. A drawn match credits everyone, because nobody was wrong. The tiebreaker measures distance from the true score in both directions equally, so overshooting is penalized exactly as much as undershooting.
sportspicker_core/engines/mma.py: A correct winner scores; naming the method as well scores more; naming the method and the round scores the jackpot. A TKO and a KO are the same outcome for prediction purposes and must score alike, because that is what anyone who follows the sport means by the pick. A fight without a FightResult, or a result naming someone who was not in the fight, raises rather than scoring zero for everyone.
sportspicker_core/strategies/base.py: A normalization strategy emits RELATIVE weights, never final points. The library turns weights into shares of the round's pot, which is what lets a strategy paying 25 and one paying 25,000 move the championship identically.
sportspicker_core/strategies/builtin.py: Each shipped strategy weighs a round without deciding its value. Rank pays by finishing position, with tied members sharing the combined value of the positions they occupy and places beyond the points table taking the tail value, which must be given and must be a non-negative number. Share is proportional to raw score. Equal credits only members who actually scored. Raw is a deliberately unnormalized baseline for measurement and must stay that way.
sportspicker_core/strategies/registry.py: Every strategy is reachable by its slug, and asking for an unknown one fails loudly rather than silently substituting a default that would change every score in the contest.
Strategy parameters are validated before they can affect a score, so a malformed points table, a missing tail value, an impossible minimum or a minimum without a mode is refused at configuration time rather than producing a plausible but wrong league table.
sportspicker_core/formats.py: Confidence points: in a round of N games a member stakes each pick with a distinct value from 1 to N, and a correct pick earns exactly its stake while a wrong one earns nothing; correctness and the tiebreaker pass through unchanged. Confidence applies only to an engine that pays 0 or 1 and agrees with its own verdict: a weighted engine (MMA pays 1, 2 or 5) or a result whose points contradict its correctness is refused, never multiplied. A stake below 1, or one that is not an integer (a bool included), is refused. A slate is valid when every value is within 1..N and none is used twice; a partial or empty slate is valid, and more values than games is not. Non-integer values or game counts raise rather than being reported as a member's mistake.
